architectureDecisions: D1 — Flag is --recovery-dir, matching deliver. Add [--recovery-dir <dir>] to the run USAGE line. parseOptions already stores hyphenated flags. commandRun reads recoveryDir = options["recovery-dir"] ?? null. When null, the current runSupervisedTask call (no recoveryDir key) is unchanged, including --trace-dir observation. DELIVERED_TRUTH: run USAGE has no --recovery-dir while deliver USAGE and commandDeliverCli already map options["recovery-dir"]; commandRun's runSupervisedTask call never passes recoveryDir. Audit at 5386e2ad: runCliPassesRecoveryDir false, supervisorAcceptsRecoveryDir true.

D2 — Resume detection in the bin only, same handle.json protocol as deliver minus QA. Import resumeSupervisedTask, RecoveryError and readAgentToolRunHandle. After resolveTool and observation: if recoveryDir is null, runSupervisedTask(launch). Else try readAgentToolRunHandle(recoveryDir); RecoveryError => existing=null. existing===null => runSupervisedTask({...launch, recoveryDir}). Else identity gate: task.id, resolve(task.repositoryRoot), task.baseRevision must equal handle.taskId/repositoryRoot/baseRevision else throw RecoveryError HANDLE_INVALID (same comparison as deliver assertSliceHandleIdentity) before resume or spawn. If status is ACCEPTED, EXHAUSTED or TOOL_UNAVAILABLE throw RecoveryError HANDLE_COMPLETE before resumeSupervisedTask. RUNNING => resumeSupervisedTask(existing, launch) with the same tool, original task JSON, model, maxAttempts, timeoutMs, permissionProfile and observation hooks. main() maps RecoveryError to stderr `${error.code}: ${error.message}` and exit 1; UsageError stays 64. CLI never calls disposeRecoverableRun. Do not extract a shared helper; do not write supervisor.js, recovery.js or deliver-slice.js.

D3 — Crash/resume fixture. packages/agent-tools/test/run-cli-recovery.test.js spawns delivered crash-supervised.mjs (CRASH_RECOVERY_DIR, CRASH_PHASE ACT_COMPLETED, fake-agent.mjs, exit 97) so handle.json is RUNNING, then spawns BIN `exharness-agent run --tool codex --command <fake-agent.mjs> --task <same.json> --recovery-dir <same>`. Assert resume status ACCEPTED, handle.worktreeRoot and coreSessionId unchanged, source repositorySnapshot (HEAD, symbolic-ref, refs/heads, porcelain, worktree count) equal before/after. P2: empty recovery dir, spawn BIN first-run with FAKE_AGENT_SCENARIO=FIX_FIRST, handle.json appears, status ACCEPTED, source snapshot unchanged. Hermetic fake CLI; no network, no credentials, no real agent CLIs.

D4 — Fail-closed bindings. N1: runSupervisedTask twice with the same recoveryDir; second throw RecoveryError HANDLE_CURRENT (`a current handle already exists`) before a second worktree add. N2: runSupervisedTask without recoveryDir still disposes the mkdtemp scratch (source worktree count unchanged, no handle.json). N3: RUNNING handle plus a task whose id differs; CLI identity gate and resumeSupervisedTask throw HANDLE_INVALID `resume task identity does not match the handle`; handle.json digest unchanged. N4: ACCEPTED handle plus `exharness-agent run --recovery-dir` / resumeSupervisedTask throw HANDLE_COMPLETE; no child spawn. Tests titled 'BB-135 N1'...'BB-135 N4' in run-cli-recovery.test.js must invoke the bound subjectSymbol.

D5 — BB-125 non-interference. Pass the original parsed --task object into runSupervisedTask and resumeSupervisedTask. Do not compute digests, persist BOUND, or throw CONTRACT_DRIFT. Worker start: commandRun still omits recoveryDir; AGENT_TOOL_RUN_HANDLE_V1 and HANDLE_CURRENT/HANDLE_COMPLETE/HANDLE_INVALID remain as delivered. Existing recovery.test.js RC1–RC5 stay green.

D6 — Living docs. docs/living/system/agent-tools/operator.md currently documents only deliver --recovery-dir; add an `exharness-agent run` section: --recovery-dir persists handle.json; missing handle starts a recoverable run; RUNNING resumes the same attempt; terminal ACCEPTED/EXHAUSTED/TOOL_UNAVAILABLE refuses HANDLE_COMPLETE; mismatched task identity refuses HANDLE_INVALID; omitting the flag keeps mkdtemp dispose; the CLI does not auto-dispose. docs/living/system/agent-tools/recovery.md states that operator run --recovery-dir composes the delivered handle/resume APIs and still contains AGENT_TOOL_RUN_HANDLE_V1. No Blackboard ids.

D7 — Evidence (discovery.json + cli-composition-audit.json at 5386e2ad, providerCalls 0): runCliPassesRecoveryDir false, supervisorAcceptsRecoveryDir true. Source: commandRun runSupervisedTask object has no recoveryDir; deliver maps options["recovery-dir"]; runRecoverableTask throws HANDLE_CURRENT when handle.json exists; resumeSupervisedTask throws HANDLE_COMPLETE for terminal status and HANDLE_INVALID on identity mismatch.
